Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, both relevant skill instructions, and the inherited rollout evidence. Then I’ll trace the assigned parent and existing policy before making a single candidate, and I’ll validate both required documentation updates.

I’m applying both requested shelves now: `read-wake-visual-signals-first` governs the evidence order and visual diagnosis, while `fish-control-primitives` will be consulted only after the metrics and keyframes are grounded. The shelf’s invariant/translation/falsification block will be recorded if it informs the edit.

The four direct-uniform rollouts agree on the missing capability: all remain self-propelled with coherent alternating wakes, yet all pass below the target and exit through the lower boundary. The best whole-body half-cycle redirect improves closest approach to `3.691L`, but its folded bearing begins releasing after the target passes abeam even though the true head-relative error grows past `2 rad`; I’m now checking the shelf’s turning sources and the detailed load/limit histories before fixing that semantic gate.

The architecture is now fixed: retain the sampled best whole-body half-cycle mechanism, but make only its activation magnitude rear-aware. The full target angle will control the gate, while the existing folded bearing supplies a continuous left/right sign, avoiding the `atan` branch as an actuation-sign discontinuity. This preserves the pre-abeam behavior and directly tests whether premature release—not another gain—is blocking recovery.

The candidate and both required knowledge artifacts are now updated. The durable lesson records the narrow positive result (`3.691L` with preserved wake), the full-angle-only negative result, and a clear boundary: semantic target geometry must sustain an actual yaw-producing residual, and further relief/asymmetry tuning is not justified if this pairing fails. I’m moving to the mandated contract and symmetry checks now; no CFD will be run.

The mandated checker role could not start because its pinned model is unavailable in this runtime. I did invoke it; I’m now running the exact three commands from its immutable contract locally, separately, and will repair any failure before finishing.

The first check exposed a rendered-workspace defect: `README.md` marks the same assigned parent twice, so the validator cannot identify exactly one baseline. Inherited worker logs document this same repair pattern. I’m removing only the duplicate marker, then rerunning the guidance check.

All mandated local checks now pass: guidance delta/notes, Julia contract and finite output, and solver boundary. An additional non-CFD test confirms reflection equivariance, exact equivalence to the best sampled controller before the target passes abeam, deliberate divergence afterward, and finite behavior on the rear axis. I’m doing the final file audit now.

Produced exactly one policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1) implements a rear-aware whole-body half-cycle redirect.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records the visual diagnosis, hypothesis, bookshelf transfer, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:60) now captures the `3.691L` positive result and full-angle-only negative boundary.
- Removed the duplicate assigned-parent marker from [README.md](README.md:123).

All non-CFD checks pass: guidance delta, Julia contract/schema, solver boundary, reflection equivariance, pre-abeam equivalence, and finite rear-axis behavior. The pinned checker agent was unavailable, so its exact commands were run locally. No CFD was run.
